headline: PBOC confirms a 1.25% overnight anchor and long-bond profit-taking lifts the 10Y CCDC to 1.65%
summary: CGBs sold off on Friday even though stocks stayed weak. The CCDC 10-year rose 2.7bp to 1.650% and the 30-year 3.6bp to 2.083%, while the 20-year led with a 4.5bp jump; on the week the 10-year is up 1.0bp, though still 3.2bp lower over the month. Policy banks fell in line: CDB 10-year rose 3.2bp to 1.693%, 4.3bp over CGB, with ADBC and EXIM about 6.9bp and 6.0bp over.
drivers: The 30-year future (TL) fell 0.94% to 117.42, its biggest one-day drop since March, with T down 0.21% and TS down 0.06%; cash yields rose 2–3bp. Desks said bonds had fully priced the good news and that demand to lock in gains on ultra-long bonds was strong, so the market overreacted to small shifts.

The PBOC said that from Nov 2 it will run overnight reverse repos every working day at a fixed 1.25%, while 7-day operations move to fixed-quantity, multiple-price tenders mainly around tax days and month-ends. Other tools will be priced off the overnight rate with unchanged spreads. The 2-year was already near 1.22–1.25%, so the confirmation brought no new easing and buyers stepped back.

The PBOC rolled RMB1tn of overnight repos and added RMB15bn of 7-day repos at 1.40%, a RMB15bn net injection. Overnight Shibor rose 0.7bp to 1.289% and 7-day 5.2bp to 1.392% into month-end, a small rise that added to the selling at the front end.
Weak stocks and soft US yields did not help

The CSI 300 headed for a 12th weekly loss, with roughly 4,450 A-shares down and about 850 up. US 10-year yields fell 6.6bp to 4.937% and the yuan held near its strongest since 2022. Those normally support CGBs, which shows positioning drove the day. Up to RMB2.2tn of net government bond supply expected in Nov–Dec also weighs on the long end.
data: Q3 PBOC loan report (Oct 28)
Property loans RMB50.08tn, −5.2% y/y; mortgages RMB35.91tn, −4.1% y/y (−1.1tn YTD)
Households keep paying down mortgages, so credit demand stays weak and banks keep buying bonds.
Sep industrial profits (Oct 27)
A beat driven by AI hardware, metals and oil-linked prices, not households; bonds looked through it.
Oct MLF (Oct 26)
RMB700bn 1Y vs RMB900bn maturing (net −200bn); outright reverse repos +400bn net in Oct
A tidy-up, not tightening: medium-term liquidity is still up RMB200bn in October, and the overnight rate is now the policy signal.
Q3 GDP (Oct 19)
Firmer growth, near the bottom of the 4.5–5% target. It eases pressure for stimulus but was not strong enough to sell bonds.
Sep activity (Oct 19)
Growth is led by exports and AI-linked output, with households and property still weak. It does not challenge low yields.
Sep CPI / PPI (Oct 14)
CPI 0.9% (f 1.0%), core 1.0%; PPI 5.0% (f 4.4–4.5%), highest since Jun 2022
Cost-push from oil and AI components, not demand. Bonds ignore it unless core CPI follows.
Sep credit (Oct 14)
New loans RMB1.08tn (f 0.98tn); TSF 3.55tn; M2 7.2% (f 7.4%); M1 3.2%
Loan growth is at a record-low 4.8% and money growth is slowing. Weak credit demand keeps banks buying bonds.
view: Neutral, leaning to buy dips, for the next 1–2 weeks, with the 10-year expected in a 1.62–1.67% CCDC range (shifted up from 1.59–1.65%). The 1.25% overnight rate is now confirmed rather than a fresh cut, ultra-long positions are crowded and Nov–Dec supply is heavy, so the rally needs a new catalyst. Weak credit, a 12-week equity slide and cheap overnight funding still limit the selloff, so I would buy 10-year CGBs near 1.65% rather than the rich 5–7Y belly or policy banks, and stay neutral on the 30-year. A soft October PMI on Saturday or more equity losses would take the 10-year back to 1.62%; a strong PMI or a heavy November supply calendar could push it to 1.67–1.68%.

buckets.name: CGB 1–2Y
buckets.why: The 2-year rose 2.4bp to 1.246%, flat on the week and in the 16th percentile of its 1-year range (average 1.311%); the 1-year at 1.171% is about 12bp below overnight Shibor (1.289%). With the overnight anchor confirmed at 1.25%, the front end has little room left to rally.
buckets.call: Hold; add 2-year CGBs only above 1.27%, or if the overnight rate is cut below 1.25%.

buckets.name: CGB 5–7Y belly
buckets.why: The 5-year rose 2.3bp to 1.353% and the 7-year 2.9bp to 1.460%, but the belly is still the richest part of the curve: 2s5s10s is −18.9bp, a 1-year low (0th percentile, average −7.5bp), and 5s7s10s is −8.4bp (2nd percentile). The 5s10s flattener from ~29bp is open at 29.7bp (91st percentile, average 26.4bp), inside the 31bp stop.
buckets.call: Keep the 5Y-into-10Y switch (5s10s flattener) from ~29bp, target 25bp, stop 31bp.

buckets.name: CGB 10Y
buckets.why: The 10-year rose 2.7bp to 1.650%, reaching the 1.645–1.65% buy level, so the long is now on. It is cheap against its neighbours: the 7s10s20s fly is −23.9bp, in the 86th percentile against a −29.3bp average, while the level is still only in the 4th percentile of the year.
buckets.call: Long from 1.65%, target 1.61%, stop 1.68%; add on a move to 1.665%.

buckets.name: CGB 30Y
buckets.why: 10s30s steepened 0.9bp to 43.3bp, in the 30th percentile and below its 45.5bp average, as the 30-year rose 3.6bp to 2.083% on profit-taking. The 20-year jumped 4.5bp to 2.079%, almost level with the 30-year, so the ultra-long sector is cheapening as a block, and supply is heavy in Nov–Dec. The 2.10% add level has not been reached.
buckets.call: Neutral. Add above 2.10% (10s30s ~46bp); poor risk/reward below 2.05%.

buckets.name: Policy banks 2–10Y vs CGB
buckets.why: CDB 10-year is 4.3bp over CGB, in the 5th percentile against a 10.0bp average, and CDB 2-year and 5-year spreads (12.3bp and 11.0bp) are in the 2nd and 11th percentiles. The switch from ~3bp is open and 1.3bp in the money, as CDB 10-year (+3.2bp) sold off slightly more than CGB.
buckets.call: Keep the CDB 10Y into CGB 10Y switch from ~3bp, target 8bp, stop 1bp.

buckets.name: ADBC/EXIM vs CDB 10Y
buckets.why: ADBC 10-year yields 2.6bp more than CDB, in the 70th percentile against a 1.3bp average; EXIM is 1.6bp over, slightly below its 2.0bp average. EXIM sold a 1-year bond at 1.3003% with 3.1x cover, so the pickup reflects supply and liquidity, not credit.
buckets.call: Hold ADBC/EXIM 10Y rather than CDB 10Y for the ~2–3bp pickup.

buckets.name: Policy banks 20–30Y
buckets.why: CDB 20-year is 4.9bp over CGB, a 1-year low (0th percentile, average 10.8bp), and the 30-year 11.0bp (17th percentile, average 12.8bp). Policy bank long bonds sold off in step with CGBs today, so the spread offers no cushion if supply picks up.
buckets.call: Prefer CGB 20–30Y to CDB 20–30Y; revisit policy bank long bonds above a 13bp 30-year spread.
